How to use this calculator

  1. Enter course 1 grade points, course 1 credits, course 2 grade points and the remaining inputs.
  2. Select Calculate to see the answer and its breakdown.
  3. Keep a scenario, change an input and compare the results.

Use consistent units and check the assumptions below before applying the result.

How gpa is calculated

Compute a weighted grade-point average from course grades and credit weights. Enter one grade point per course and its credit value; total quality points are divided by total credits. This calculator does not assume a country’s grading scale, so translate grades to your institution’s scale first. A 3-credit course at 4.0 and a 1-credit course at 3.0 produce (12+3)/4 = 3.75. The calculation validates each input and keeps its stated units explicit. Yes, credits weight each course; equal weighting is appropriate only when course credits are equal. This is an estimate for the stated assumptions; confirm measurements and any applicable professional or local standards before relying on it.

GPA = Σ(grade points × credits) ÷ Σ credits
A worked example

A 3-credit course at 4.0 and a 1-credit course at 3.0 produce (12+3)/4 = 3.75.

Assumptions & useful context

The result depends on the values you enter and the method described above. Displayed numbers may be rounded; calculations use the unrounded values. Check that this model matches your situation before relying on it.

Frequently asked questions

Does GPA use course credits?

Yes, credits weight each course; equal weighting is appropriate only when course credits are equal.

Can I enter percentages directly?

Only if your institution defines those numbers as grade points. Convert letter or percentage grades first.
